newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine judge in love motel scandal.
newsitem.headline: Argentine judge in love motel scandal.

text.p: An Argentine judge will be impeached after reports he was involved in a scandalous episode in a pay-by-the-hour "love hotel", Justice Minister Elias Jassan said on Wednesday.
"This is a very unfortunate situation. This sort of conduct is misconduct," Jassan told the state-run Telam news agency. "He is going to have to face the consequences of impeachment."

He was speaking after Argentine media reported an alleged incident which began when 62-year-old Judge Jose Luis Ramos, accompanied by a young woman, rented a $45-an-hour suite in a Buenos Aires "love hotel" in February.
The woman left soon afterwards, but Ramos stayed behind and got into an argument with the concierge, allegedly hitting him several times with an empty champagne bottle.
The top-selling Clarin daily quoted unidentified investigation sources as saying the judge threatened to send the hotel staff to prison.
Ramos confronted a policeman called by the hotel management, snatched his cap and knocked him down, Clarin said.
No police spokesman was immediately available to confirm the comments. Reporters who went to Ramos's house to seek comment were told by his wife he no longer lived there.
